questions.questionText: Which tissue type lines the inner surface of the mouth?
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines body cavities, providing protection and absorption.

questions.questionText: Which tissue type is responsible for movement in animals?
questions.explanation: Muscle tissue contracts to produce movement and is classified into skeletal, smooth, and cardiac types.

questions.questionText: Which plant tissue is responsible for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Palisade mesophyll cells contain many chloroplasts and are the primary site of photosynthesis in plant leaves.

questions.questionText: Which type of blood cell is responsible for fighting infection?
questions.explanation: White blood cells (leucocytes) defend the body against pathogens and are a key part of the immune system.

questions.questionText: Which nerve tissue type carries impulses from the brain to effectors?
questions.explanation: Motor neurons carry nerve impulses from the CNS to effectors (muscles or glands) to produce responses.

questions.questionText: Meristematic tissue in plants is characterised by:
questions.explanation: Meristematic tissues contain undifferentiated cells that continuously divide, producing new cells for plant growth.

questions.questionText: Which tissue connects bones to bones?
questions.explanation: Ligaments are dense connective tissue bands that connect bones to other bones at joints, providing stability.

questions.questionText: Which type of epithelial tissue is found in the alveoli of lungs?
questions.explanation: Simple squamous epithelium is thin and flattened, ideal for rapid diffusion of gases across the alveolar walls.

questions.questionText: Skeletal muscle is described as:
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle is voluntary (under conscious control) and striated (has alternating light and dark bands) due to actin and myosin arrangement.

questions.questionText: Which tissue type has the most extracellular matrix?
questions.explanation: Connective tissue is characterised by having cells scattered within abundant extracellular matrix containing fibres and ground substance.

questions.questionText: Which plant tissue transports water from roots to leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels transport water and dissolved minerals from roots to all parts of the plant through capillary action and transpiration pull.

questions.questionText: Cardiac muscle is found in:
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart wall, where it contracts rhythmically and continuously to pump blood.

questions.questionText: Permanent tissues in plants:

options.text: Have differentiated cells that have lost the ability to divide
Are the same as meristematic tissue

questions.explanation: Permanent tissues consist of differentiated cells that have assumed specific functions and no longer divide, unlike meristematic tissue.

questions.questionText: Which tissue type responds to stimuli by generating electrical signals?
questions.explanation: Nerve tissue (neurons and neuroglia) responds to stimuli and generates electrical impulses for communication within the body.

questions.questionText: Areolar connective tissue differs from adipose tissue because areolar tissue:

options.text: Stores fat and has little matrix
Binds tissues together and has a gel-like matrix with fibres
Is found only in the heart
Contains more fat cells than collagen

questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue with a gel-like ground substance and various fibres that fills spaces between organs and binds skin to muscles.

questions.questionText: Which cells in nerve tissue are involved in myelin formation in the CNS?
questions.explanation: Oligodendrocytes form myelin sheaths around axons in the central nervous system (CNS), while Schwann cells do this in the PNS.

questions.questionText: The key difference between smooth muscle and skeletal muscle is:

options.text: Smooth muscle is involuntary with no striations
Smooth muscle is voluntary with striations
Smooth muscle is found in the heart

questions.diagram: Smooth muscle is involuntary (controlled by the autonomic nervous system), non-striated, and found in walls of hollow organs like blood vessels and intestines.

questions.questionText: Cork cells in plants are impervious to water because they have:
questions.explanation: Cork cells contain suberin, a waxy substance that waterproofs the cell walls, preventing water loss and protecting the plant.

questions.questionText: The epidermis of a leaf is covered by a waxy cuticle primarily to:

options.text: Allow light to enter for photosynthesis

questions.explanation: The waxy cuticle on the epidermis forms a waterproof barrier that minimises transpiration and prevents excessive water loss.

questions.questionText: A neuron has a long axon and multiple dendrites. This structure is best suited for:

options.text: Carrying impulses over long distances and receiving signals

questions.explanation: The long axon carries impulses away from the cell body over distances, while multiple dendrites receive signals from other neurons.
